quotes.text: Here's the honest deal. Sharepoints are great at one thing, collecting and storing stuff, tasks, issues, milestones, risks. You can keep tossing rows and columns in and it feels user friendly enough.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clearly names what SharePoint lists are good at before explaining their limits.

quotes.text: And that's the key point here. The problem is not the data, it's the way we're forced to look at it
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Summarizes the episode's central diagnosis in one sentence.

quotes.text: The worst mistake here is thinking you need to keep everything you don't. The fewer fields you drag forward, the faster your model runs, and the cleaner the visuals look.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A practical, transferable rule for Power Query data cleanup.

quotes.text: Embedding doesn't bypass permissions. If someone can't access the report in Powerbi service, they won't magically see it in SharePoint.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clarifies a common security misconception about embedded reports.

quotes.text: Share Point lists aren't broken, they're just static. Left on their own, they trap people in endless grids and push everyone back to the export to excel reflex.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A crisp closing thesis on why lists need a reporting layer.

Publishing and embedding back into SharePoint
Wrap-up: from static lists to answers

takeaways: SharePoint lists are built for storing data, not analysis, which is why filtering, trust and scale break down and users fall back to exporting to Excel.
Connect lists with the SharePoint Online list connector in Power BI Desktop using only the site URL, then clean person, choice, lookup and UTC date fields in Power Query.
Publish to a shared workspace, grant access through groups, check Pro or Premium licensing and row-level security, and embed the report on the SharePoint page your team already uses.
hook: Tired of scrolling endless SharePoint lists and exporting to Excel just to answer a simple question? This episode is for Microsoft 365 users and admins who track work in SharePoint lists. Learn how to connect, clean, publish and embed Power BI reports so the data finally tells a story where your team already works.
